title: Gene coexpression analysis in Arabidopsis thaliana based on public microarray data
author: Zogopoulos, Malatras, et al.

steps.title: Generate PPI network with STRING
steps.instruction: Create a protein‑protein interaction network for the co‑expressed gene list using the STRING web server.

substeps.instruction: Open a web browser and go to https://string-db.org/.
Click the “Search” button.
Select “Multiple Proteins”.
Copy the entire contents of the file subtree_gene_list.txt (generated in earlier analysis) and paste them into the “List Of Names” field.
Choose “Arabidopsis thaliana” as the organism.
Click “Search”, then click “Continue” to submit the list.
When the resulting PPI network appears, open the “Analysis” tab to view “Network Stats” (density) and “Functional enrichments in your network” (predominant biological terms).
Optionally, open the “Settings” tab to adjust interaction sources and interaction thresholds.

steps.title: Run enrichment analysis with WebGestalt
steps.instruction: Perform over‑representation enrichment analysis on the same gene list using the WebGestalt platform.

substeps.instruction: Open a web browser and go to http://www.webgestalt.org/.
In the “Basic Parameters” section:
• Select “Arabidopsis thaliana” as the Organism of Interest.
• Choose “Over‑representation analysis (ORA)” as the Method of Interest.
• Click the plus (+) sign to add all available Functional Databases (or a chosen subset).
In the “Gene List” section:
• Set “Gene Symbol” as the GeneID type.
• Paste the contents of subtree_gene_list.txt into the provided box.
In the “Reference Gene List” section:
• Set “Gene Symbol” as the GeneID type.
• Choose “Upload Gene List” and upload the file ACT/data/selected_genes.txt.
Click “Submit” to run the analysis.
After completion, click the “Table” tab to view the enriched biological terms associated with the co‑expressed genes in the subtree.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for performing gene coexpression analysis on Arabidopsis thaliana Affymetrix microarray data. The same protocol can be used for any species, provided that at least 20 samples of the same Affymetrix chip are available (Langfelder and Horvath, 2017). By examining the gene coexpression tree created by following this protocol, hypotheses for gene partnership and pathway participation can be made, which can be, in turn, experimentally validated. The advantages described in this protocol include: the hierarchical clustering approach for displaying gene coexpression which outperforms the more commonly used gene coexpression list output (Obayashi et al., 2018; Yim et al., 2013), the automatic quality control procedure and the meticulous representative sample selection which eliminates tissue bias, as well as the usage of modern normalization algorithms along with up-to-date CDFs. Execution of this protocol has resulted in several use-cases, where a gene of interest was discovered to be grouped with genes of similar functions, which are supported by already existing bibliography (Zogopoulos et al., 2021).
